claim: At the exact retained Erdős statement snapshot and OpenAI ten-proofs commit 29362184c2b698c1b279bc85b3957ee813646c63, TwoDegenerateGraphs.DegeneracyConjectureStatement faithfully formalizes the meaningful positive-r domain of Erdős problem 146, and twoDegenerateExtremalCounterexample supplies the manuscript's connected bipartite 2-degenerate counterexample with an eventual exponent strictly above 3/2.

retained_problem_statement.statement: If H is bipartite and r-degenerate, meaning every induced subgraph has minimum degree at most r, then ex(n;H) is O(n^(2-1/r)).

manuscript.reference: Chapter 10, Section 1.2, equation (3), and Theorem 1.2, printed pages 235-236; PDF pages 237-238

reproduction_evidence.observed: The exact profile passed Comparator, Nanoda, and Lean's default kernel in the retained hardened network-disabled Linux replay; both declarations depend exactly on propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound.

evidence: The retained statement defines r-degeneracy through every induced subgraph having a vertex of degree at most r.
IsDegenerate r G quantifies over every nonempty finite vertex set s and requires one v in s with at most r neighbors inside s, exactly the induced-subgraph formulation.
The manuscript uses every nonempty subgraph rather than induced subgraph; these formulations are equivalent because deleting edges cannot increase vertex degree.
SimpleGraph.extremalNumber uses H.Free, where Free means that H has no subgraph copy in the host, matching the retained extremal-number convention.
DegeneracyConjectureStatement quantifies over every natural r, finite order q, and simple graph H on Fin q.
Finite simple graphs are represented up to relabeling by a graph on some Fin q, and Mathlib extremalNumber is invariant under graph isomorphism.
Lean explicitly assumes 0 < r. The retained exponent 2-1/r has no meaningful r=0 interpretation, so this makes the intended positive-r domain explicit rather than narrowing a defined case.
Asymptotics.IsBigO atTop expresses the retained eventual constant-factor upper bound.
The conjecture predicate assumes exactly positive r, bipartiteness, and r-degeneracy; it does not add connectedness or a degree condition.
The counterexample is stronger than required: H is connected, bipartite, and 2-degenerate.
The additional bipartition-side maximum-degree property in twoDegenerateExtremalCounterexample is extra witness information and is not used to redefine the conjecture.
For r=2, the conjectured exponent is 2-1/2=3/2.
The Lean witness supplies c>0 and epsilon>0 with c*n^(3/2+epsilon) at most ex(n,H) for all sufficiently large n, matching manuscript Theorem 1.2.
not_erdos_146 derives the contradiction with the conjectured Big-O bound and therefore proves the negation of the exact conjecture predicate.
